synopsis: These formats enable simulation tools to exchange scene, road, surface, scenario, label and operating-domain descriptions; alongside OSI and FMI, they serve as integration glue, but compatibility does not establish physical fidelity [f13196, f8335, f13214]. OpenUSD is domain-neutral and can represent mines and construction sites, whereas OpenDRIVE assumes road networks and fits sites without lanes poorly; stockpiles, berms, ruts and other off-road features often need additional representations [f8610, f3982, f8724]. The cited releases include OpenODD 1.0.0 on 3 April 2025, OpenSCENARIO DSL 2.2.0 on 19 March 2026, OpenDRIVE 1.9.0 in May 2026, and OpenSCENARIO XML 1.4.0 in 2026, with June reported by a secondary listing [f6707, f7152, f7156, f7149]. OpenODD and related ISO structures are useful architectural templates, but their road-oriented scope and attributes require a manufacturer- or industry-governed off-road taxonomy [f6642, f6709, f7163]. Off-road scenario standardisation remains incomplete, with missing concepts including deformable terrain, particles, vegetation, heavy-machine manipulation and sensor degradation; the booklet anticipates extensions being unlikely before mid-2027, rather than treating OpenX as unusable [f7432, f7195, f7172, f7196]. The recommended approach is a manufacturer-owned, domain-neutral, version-controlled scenario catalogue, OpenDRIVE for structured haul roads, OpenUSD and OpenMATERIAL for scenes, and OpenSCENARIO exports where required, with open-format exports and exit clauses protecting against supplier dependence [f13215, f13216, f8887].
